raw: Act 3, Scene 5 — An open Gallery to Juliet’s Chamber, overlooking the Garden
Enter Romeo and Juliet.

speaker: JULIET
raw:
Wilt thou be gone? It is not yet near day.
It was the nightingale, and not the lark,
That pierc’d the fearful hollow of thine ear;
Nightly she sings on yond pomegranate tree.
Believe me, love, it was the nightingale.

gemma4_gloss.en: Will you leave?
It is not near day yet.
It was the nightingale, and not the lark, that entered your fearful ear.
She sings every night on that pomegranate tree over there.
Believe me, love, it was the nightingale.

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
It was the lark, the herald of the morn,
No nightingale. Look, love, what envious streaks
Do lace the severing clouds in yonder east.
Night’s candles are burnt out, and jocund day
Stands tiptoe on the misty mountain tops.
I must be gone and live, or stay and die.

gemma4_gloss.en: It was the lark, the herald of the morning, not a nightingale.
Look, love, at the jealous streaks that cross the clouds in the east over there.
The candles of night are burned out.
And the happy day stands on tiptoe on the misty mountain tops.
I must leave and live, or stay and die.

speaker: JULIET
raw:
Yond light is not daylight, I know it, I.
It is some meteor that the sun exhales
To be to thee this night a torchbearer
And light thee on thy way to Mantua.
Therefore stay yet, thou need’st not to be gone.

gemma4_gloss.en: That light is not daylight, I know it.
It is some meteor that the sun breathes out.
It is to be a torchbearer for you tonight.
It will light your way to Mantua.
Therefore stay now. You do not need to leave.

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
Let me be ta’en, let me be put to death,
I am content, so thou wilt have it so.
I’ll say yon grey is not the morning’s eye,
’Tis but the pale reflex of Cynthia’s brow.
Nor that is not the lark whose notes do beat
The vaulty heaven so high above our heads.
I have more care to stay than will to go.
Come, death, and welcome. Juliet wills it so.
How is’t, my soul? Let’s talk. It is not day.

gemma4_gloss.en: Let me be caught. Let me be put to death.
I am content, if you want it that way.
I will say that gray light is not the morning's eye.
It is only the pale reflection of Cynthia's brow.
That is not the lark whose notes beat the high vault of heaven above our heads.
I care more to stay than I want to go.
Come, death, and welcome me. Juliet wants it so.
How are you, my soul? Let's talk.
It is not day.

speaker: JULIET
raw:
It is, it is! Hie hence, be gone, away.
It is the lark that sings so out of tune,
Straining harsh discords and unpleasing sharps.
Some say the lark makes sweet division;
This doth not so, for she divideth us.
Some say the lark and loathed toad change eyes.
O, now I would they had chang’d voices too,
Since arm from arm that voice doth us affray,
Hunting thee hence with hunt’s-up to the day.
O now be gone, more light and light it grows.

gemma4_gloss.en: It is, it is!
Hurry away! Go now!
It is the lark that sings out of tune.
It makes harsh sounds and unpleasant notes.
Some say the lark makes sweet music.
This does not do so, because she separates us.
Some say the lark and the hated toad change eyes.
Oh, I wish they had changed voices too.
That voice scares us apart from arm to arm.
It hunts you away toward the day.
Oh, now go. The light is growing more and more.

speaker: ROMEO
raw: More light and light, more dark and dark our woes.

gemma4_gloss.en: More light and light, more dark and dark our woes.

raw: Enter Nurse.

speaker: NURSE
raw: Madam.

gemma4_gloss.en: Madam.

speaker: JULIET
raw: Nurse?

gemma4_gloss.en: Nurse?

speaker: NURSE
raw:
Your lady mother is coming to your chamber.
The day is broke, be wary, look about.

gemma4_gloss.en: Your mother is coming to your room.
The day has started.
Be careful and look around.

raw: Exit.

speaker: JULIET
raw: Then, window, let day in, and let life out.

gemma4_gloss.en: Then, window, let the day in.
Let life go out.

speaker: ROMEO
raw: Farewell, farewell, one kiss, and I’ll descend.

gemma4_gloss.en: Goodbye.
Give me one kiss.
Then I will go down.

raw: Descends.

gemma4_gloss.en: Romeo descends.

speaker: JULIET
raw:
Art thou gone so? Love, lord, ay husband, friend,
I must hear from thee every day in the hour,
For in a minute there are many days.
O, by this count I shall be much in years
Ere I again behold my Romeo.

gemma4_gloss.en: Are you gone so soon?
My love, my lord, my husband, and my friend, I must hear from you every day in the hour.
Because there are many days in a single minute.
By this count, I will be much older before I see my Romeo again.

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
Farewell!
I will omit no opportunity
That may convey my greetings, love, to thee.

gemma4_gloss.en: Goodbye!
I will not miss any chance to send my greetings and my love to you.

speaker: JULIET
raw: O thinkest thou we shall ever meet again?

gemma4_gloss.en: Do you think we will ever meet again?

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
I doubt it not, and all these woes shall serve
For sweet discourses in our time to come.

gemma4_gloss.en: I do not doubt it.
All these sorrows will serve as sweet stories for us to tell in the future.

speaker: JULIET
raw:
O God! I have an ill-divining soul!
Methinks I see thee, now thou art so low,
As one dead in the bottom of a tomb.
Either my eyesight fails, or thou look’st pale.

gemma4_gloss.en: Oh God!
I have a soul that predicts bad things.
I think I see you now.
You are so low.
You look like someone dead at the bottom of a tomb.
Either my eyesight is failing, or you look pale.

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
And trust me, love, in my eye so do you.
Dry sorrow drinks our blood. Adieu, adieu.

gemma4_gloss.en: Trust me, love.
You look that way in my eyes too.
Dry sorrow drinks our blood.
Goodbye, goodbye.

raw: Exit below.

gemma4_gloss.en: Romeo exits below.

speaker: JULIET
raw:
O Fortune, Fortune! All men call thee fickle,
If thou art fickle, what dost thou with him
That is renown’d for faith? Be fickle, Fortune;
For then, I hope thou wilt not keep him long
But send him back.

gemma4_gloss.en: Oh Fortune, Fortune!
All men call you fickle.
If you are fickle, what do you do with him?
He is famous for his faith.
Be fickle, Fortune.
Then, I hope you will not keep him long.
I hope you send him back.

speaker: LADY CAPULET
raw: Ho, daughter, are you up?

gemma4_gloss.en: Hey, daughter, are you awake?

speaker: JULIET
raw:
Who is’t that calls? Is it my lady mother?
Is she not down so late, or up so early?
What unaccustom’d cause procures her hither?

gemma4_gloss.en: Who is calling?
Is it my lady mother?
Is she not down so late or up so early?
What unusual reason brings her here?

raw: Enter Lady Capulet.

speaker: LADY CAPULET
raw: Why, how now, Juliet?

gemma4_gloss.en: Well, how are you now, Juliet?

speaker: JULIET
raw: Madam, I am not well.

gemma4_gloss.en: Madam, I am not well.

speaker: LADY CAPULET
raw:
Evermore weeping for your cousin’s death?
What, wilt thou wash him from his grave with tears?
And if thou couldst, thou couldst not make him live.
Therefore have done: some grief shows much of love,
But much of grief shows still some want of wit.

gemma4_gloss.en: Are you still crying for your cousin's death?
Will you wash him from his grave with your tears?
Even if you could, you could not make him live.
Stop now.
Some grief shows a lot of love.
But too much grief shows a lack of intelligence.

speaker: JULIET
raw: Yet let me weep for such a feeling loss.

gemma4_gloss.en: Still, let me weep for such a great loss.

speaker: LADY CAPULET
raw:
So shall you feel the loss, but not the friend
Which you weep for.

gemma4_gloss.en: You will feel the loss.
But you are not crying for the friend.

speaker: JULIET
raw:
Feeling so the loss,
I cannot choose but ever weep the friend.

gemma4_gloss.en: Because I feel this loss, I cannot help but always weep for my friend.

speaker: LADY CAPULET
raw:
Well, girl, thou weep’st not so much for his death
As that the villain lives which slaughter’d him.

gemma4_gloss.en: Well, girl, you do not cry so much for his death.
You cry because the villain who killed him is still alive.

speaker: JULIET
raw: What villain, madam?

gemma4_gloss.en: What villain, madam?

speaker: LADY CAPULET
raw: That same villain Romeo.

gemma4_gloss.en: That same villain, Romeo.

speaker: JULIET
raw:
Villain and he be many miles asunder.
God pardon him. I do, with all my heart.
And yet no man like he doth grieve my heart.

gemma4_gloss.en: He is a villain and he is many miles away.
God forgive him.
I forgive him with all my heart.
And yet no man causes me more pain than he does.

speaker: LADY CAPULET
raw: That is because the traitor murderer lives.

gemma4_gloss.en: That is because the traitor and murderer is still alive.

speaker: JULIET
raw:
Ay madam, from the reach of these my hands.
Would none but I might venge my cousin’s death.

gemma4_gloss.en: Yes, madam, I cannot reach him with my hands.
I wish only I could take revenge for my cousin's death.

speaker: LADY CAPULET
raw:
We will have vengeance for it, fear thou not.
Then weep no more. I’ll send to one in Mantua,
Where that same banish’d runagate doth live,
Shall give him such an unaccustom’d dram
That he shall soon keep Tybalt company:
And then I hope thou wilt be satisfied.

gemma4_gloss.en: We will have revenge for it. Do not fear.
Stop crying now.
I will send a message to someone in Mantua.
That banished criminal lives there.
He will give him a strange drink.
It will make him join Tybalt in death soon.
Then I hope you will be satisfied.

speaker: JULIET
raw:
Indeed I never shall be satisfied
With Romeo till I behold him—dead—
Is my poor heart so for a kinsman vex’d.
Madam, if you could find out but a man
To bear a poison, I would temper it,
That Romeo should upon receipt thereof,
Soon sleep in quiet. O, how my heart abhors
To hear him nam’d, and cannot come to him,
To wreak the love I bore my cousin
Upon his body that hath slaughter’d him.

gemma4_gloss.en: I will never be satisfied with Romeo until I see him dead.
Is my poor heart so upset for a relative?
Madam, if you could find just one man to carry a poison, I would mix it.
Romeo would fall asleep forever as soon as he received it.
Oh, how much I hate to hear his name.
I cannot reach him.
I want to take my love for my cousin out on his body.
He is the one who killed him.

speaker: LADY CAPULET
raw:
Find thou the means, and I’ll find such a man.
But now I’ll tell thee joyful tidings, girl.

gemma4_gloss.en: If you find a way, I will find such a man.
But now I have happy news for you, girl.

speaker: JULIET
raw:
And joy comes well in such a needy time.
What are they, I beseech your ladyship?

gemma4_gloss.en: Joy comes at a good time during such a sad time.
What is the news, I beg of your ladyship?

speaker: LADY CAPULET
raw:
Well, well, thou hast a careful father, child;
One who to put thee from thy heaviness,
Hath sorted out a sudden day of joy,
That thou expects not, nor I look’d not for.

gemma4_gloss.en: Well, you have a very caring father, child.
He has planned a sudden day of joy to cheer you up.
You did not expect it, and I did not expect it either.

speaker: JULIET
raw: Madam, in happy time, what day is that?

gemma4_gloss.en: Madam, in such happy times, what day is it?

speaker: LADY CAPULET
raw:
Marry, my child, early next Thursday morn
The gallant, young, and noble gentleman,
The County Paris, at Saint Peter’s Church,
Shall happily make thee there a joyful bride.

gemma4_gloss.en: Yes, my child.
Early next Thursday morning, the brave and noble young man, count Paris, will marry you at Saint Peter's Church.
He will make you a happy bride there.

speaker: JULIET
raw:
Now by Saint Peter’s Church, and Peter too,
He shall not make me there a joyful bride.
I wonder at this haste, that I must wed
Ere he that should be husband comes to woo.
I pray you tell my lord and father, madam,
I will not marry yet; and when I do, I swear
It shall be Romeo, whom you know I hate,
Rather than Paris. These are news indeed.

gemma4_gloss.en: I swear by Saint Peter's Church and by Saint Peter himself.
He will not make me a happy bride.
I am surprised by this hurry.
I must marry before the man who should be my husband can try to win my love.
Please tell my father, madam.
I will not marry yet.
When I do marry, I promise it will be Romeo.
You know that I hate him.
I would rather marry him than Paris.
This is truly news.

speaker: LADY CAPULET
raw:
Here comes your father, tell him so yourself,
And see how he will take it at your hands.

gemma4_gloss.en: Your father is coming here.
Tell him the truth yourself.
See how he reacts to your words.

raw: Enter Capulet and Nurse.

speaker: CAPULET
raw:
When the sun sets, the air doth drizzle dew;
But for the sunset of my brother’s son
It rains downright.
How now? A conduit, girl? What, still in tears?
Evermore showering? In one little body
Thou counterfeits a bark, a sea, a wind.
For still thy eyes, which I may call the sea,
Do ebb and flow with tears; the bark thy body is,
Sailing in this salt flood, the winds, thy sighs,
Who raging with thy tears and they with them,
Without a sudden calm will overset
Thy tempest-tossed body. How now, wife?
Have you deliver’d to her our decree?

gemma4_gloss.en: When the sun sets, the air produces dew.
But for the sunset of my brother's son, it rains heavily.
What is it, girl?
Are you holding a container?
Are you still crying?
Are you always crying?
In your small body, you act like a boat, a sea, and a wind.
Your eyes are like the sea.
They flow with tears.
Your body is like a boat.
It sails in this salty flood of tears.
Your sighs are like the winds.
The winds rage with your tears.
The tears move with the wind.
Without a sudden calm, the storm will sink your body.
What is it, wife?
Have you told her our decision?

speaker: LADY CAPULET
raw:
Ay, sir; but she will none, she gives you thanks.
I would the fool were married to her grave.

gemma4_gloss.en: Yes, sir.
But she refuses.
She gives you thanks.
I wish the fool were married to her grave.

speaker: CAPULET
raw:
Soft. Take me with you, take me with you, wife.
How, will she none? Doth she not give us thanks?
Is she not proud? Doth she not count her blest,
Unworthy as she is, that we have wrought
So worthy a gentleman to be her bridegroom?

gemma4_gloss.en: Wait.
Take me with you, wife.
How? She refuses?
Does she not thank us?
Is she not proud?
Does she not count her blessings?
Even though she is unworthy, we found such a worthy gentleman to be her groom?

speaker: JULIET

gemma4_gloss.en: She is not proud.
She is thankful for what you have.
I can never be proud of what I hate.
But I am thankful even for hate that means love.

speaker: CAPULET
raw:
How now, how now, chopp’d logic? What is this?
Proud, and, I thank you, and I thank you not;
And yet not proud. Mistress minion you,
Thank me no thankings, nor proud me no prouds,
But fettle your fine joints ’gainst Thursday next
To go with Paris to Saint Peter’s Church,
Or I will drag thee on a hurdle thither.
Out, you green-sickness carrion! Out, you baggage!
You tallow-face!

gemma4_gloss.en: What is this?
This logic is confusing.
You are proud, and you thank me, and you do not thank me.
And yet you are not proud.
You are my favorite lady.
Do not thank me for being proud or not being proud.
Prepare your fine clothes for next Thursday.
Go with Paris to Saint Peter's Church.
Or I will drag you there on a litter.
Get out, you sickly corpse!
You are just baggage!
You fat-faced woman!

speaker: LADY CAPULET
raw: Fie, fie! What, are you mad?

gemma4_gloss.en: Shame on you!
Shame on you!
Are you mad?

speaker: JULIET
raw:
Good father, I beseech you on my knees,
Hear me with patience but to speak a word.

gemma4_gloss.en: Good father, I beg you on my knees.
Listen to me patiently.
Let me speak just one word.

speaker: CAPULET
raw:
Hang thee young baggage, disobedient wretch!
I tell thee what,—get thee to church a Thursday,
Or never after look me in the face.
Speak not, reply not, do not answer me.
My fingers itch. Wife, we scarce thought us blest
That God had lent us but this only child;
But now I see this one is one too much,
And that we have a curse in having her.
Out on her, hilding.

gemma4_gloss.en: Hang you, you disobedient girl!
I tell you what.
Go to church this Thursday.
Or never look at my face again.
Do not speak.
Do not reply.
Do not answer me.
My fingers itch.
Wife, we were lucky that God gave us this only child.
But now I see she is too much for us.
Having her is a curse.
Get out of my way, girl.

speaker: NURSE
raw:
God in heaven bless her.
You are to blame, my lord, to rate her so.

gemma4_gloss.en: May God in heaven bless her.
You are to blame, my lord, for speaking to her so harshly.

speaker: CAPULET
raw:
And why, my lady wisdom? Hold your tongue,
Good prudence; smatter with your gossips, go.

gemma4_gloss.en: And why, my lady wisdom?
Hold your tongue, good prudence.
Go talk with your friends.

speaker: NURSE
raw: I speak no treason.

gemma4_gloss.en: I am not saying anything rebellious.

speaker: CAPULET
raw: O God ye good-en!

gemma4_gloss.en: Oh God, you are kind!

speaker: NURSE
raw: May not one speak?

gemma4_gloss.en: May I not speak?

speaker: CAPULET
raw:
Peace, you mumbling fool!
Utter your gravity o’er a gossip’s bowl,
For here we need it not.

gemma4_gloss.en: Be quiet, you foolish person!
Say your serious words over a gossip's bowl.
We do not need them here.

speaker: LADY CAPULET
raw: You are too hot.

gemma4_gloss.en: You are being too angry.

speaker: CAPULET
raw:
God’s bread, it makes me mad!
Day, night, hour, ride, time, work, play,
Alone, in company, still my care hath been
To have her match’d, and having now provided
A gentleman of noble parentage,
Of fair demesnes, youthful, and nobly allied,
Stuff’d, as they say, with honourable parts,
Proportion’d as one’s thought would wish a man,
And then to have a wretched puling fool,
A whining mammet, in her fortune’s tender,
To answer, ‘I’ll not wed, I cannot love,
I am too young, I pray you pardon me.’
But, and you will not wed, I’ll pardon you.
Graze where you will, you shall not house with me.
Look to’t, think on’t, I do not use to jest.
Thursday is near; lay hand on heart, advise.
And you be mine, I’ll give you to my friend;
And you be not, hang, beg, starve, die in the streets,
For by my soul, I’ll ne’er acknowledge thee,
Nor what is mine shall never do thee good.
Trust to’t, bethink you, I’ll not be forsworn.

gemma4_gloss.en: Oh, this makes me mad!
Day, night, hour, ride, time, work, play.
Alone or in company, my only concern has been to find her a husband.
I have now found a gentleman of noble parents.
He is handsome, young, and from a good family.
He has many honorable qualities.
He is exactly the kind of man I wanted.
And then to have a foolish girl crying like a baby.
She acts like a whining doll in her early life.
She says, 'I will not marry, I cannot love.'
She says, 'I am too young, please forgive me.'
But if you will not marry, I will forgive you.
Go where you want, but you will not live with me.
Think about it. I am not joking.
Thursday is near. Put your hand on your heart and decide.
If you are mine, I will give you to my friend.
If you are not mine, hang, beg, starve, or die in the streets.
I swear by my soul that I will never acknowledge you.
Nothing of mine will ever help you.
Trust me. Think about it. I will not break my promise.

raw: Exit.

speaker: JULIET
raw:
Is there no pity sitting in the clouds,
That sees into the bottom of my grief?
O sweet my mother, cast me not away,
Delay this marriage for a month, a week,
Or, if you do not, make the bridal bed
In that dim monument where Tybalt lies.

gemma4_gloss.en: Is there no pity in the clouds?
Does anyone see how sad I am?
Oh sweet mother, do not cast me away.
Delay this marriage for a month or a week.
Or, if you do not, make the wedding bed in that dark monument where Tybalt lies.

speaker: LADY CAPULET
raw:
Talk not to me, for I’ll not speak a word.
Do as thou wilt, for I have done with thee.

gemma4_gloss.en: Do not talk to me. I will not say a word.
Do what you want. I am finished with you.

raw: Exit.

speaker: JULIET
raw:
O God! O Nurse, how shall this be prevented?
My husband is on earth, my faith in heaven.
How shall that faith return again to earth,
Unless that husband send it me from heaven
By leaving earth? Comfort me, counsel me.
Alack, alack, that heaven should practise stratagems
Upon so soft a subject as myself.
What say’st thou? Hast thou not a word of joy?
Some comfort, Nurse.

gemma4_gloss.en: Oh God! Oh Nurse, how can we stop this?
My husband is on earth, and my faith is in heaven.
How will that faith return to earth?
Unless that husband sends it to me from heaven by leaving earth?
Comfort me. Give me advice.
Oh no, that heaven should use tricks on a person as gentle as myself.
What do you say?
Do you not have a word of joy?
Give me some comfort, Nurse.

speaker: NURSE
raw:
Faith, here it is.
Romeo is banished; and all the world to nothing
That he dares ne’er come back to challenge you.
Or if he do, it needs must be by stealth.
Then, since the case so stands as now it doth,
I think it best you married with the County.
O, he’s a lovely gentleman.
Romeo’s a dishclout to him. An eagle, madam,
Hath not so green, so quick, so fair an eye
As Paris hath. Beshrew my very heart,
I think you are happy in this second match,
For it excels your first: or if it did not,
Your first is dead, or ’twere as good he were,
As living here and you no use of him.

gemma4_gloss.en: Well, here it is.
Romeo is banished.
The whole world means nothing if he dares never come back to challenge you.
Or if he does, it must be in secret.
Since the situation is as it is now, I think it is best that you marry the County.
Oh, he is a lovely gentleman.
Romeo is nothing compared to him.
An eagle does not have such green, quick, and beautiful eyes as Paris has.
Curse my heart!
I think you will be happy in this second marriage.
It is better than your first one.
If it is not, your first husband is dead.
It would be just as good if he were alive here and you did not use him.

speaker: JULIET
raw: Speakest thou from thy heart?

gemma4_gloss.en: Do you speak from your heart?

speaker: NURSE
raw:
And from my soul too,
Or else beshrew them both.

gemma4_gloss.en: And I speak from my soul.
Otherwise, may they both be cursed.

speaker: JULIET
raw: Amen.

gemma4_gloss.en: Amen.

speaker: NURSE
raw: What?

gemma4_gloss.en: What?

speaker: JULIET
raw:
Well, thou hast comforted me marvellous much.
Go in, and tell my lady I am gone,
Having displeas’d my father, to Lawrence’ cell,
To make confession and to be absolv’d.

gemma4_gloss.en: Well, you have comforted me very much.
Go in and tell my lady that I am gone.
I have upset my father.
I am going to Lawrence's cell.
I must go to confess and be absolved.

speaker: NURSE
raw: Marry, I will; and this is wisely done.

gemma4_gloss.en: Indeed, I will do that.
This is a wise thing to do.

raw: Exit.

speaker: JULIET
raw:
Ancient damnation! O most wicked fiend!
Is it more sin to wish me thus forsworn,
Or to dispraise my lord with that same tongue
Which she hath prais’d him with above compare
So many thousand times? Go, counsellor.
Thou and my bosom henceforth shall be twain.
I’ll to the Friar to know his remedy.
If all else fail, myself have power to die.

gemma4_gloss.en: Ancient damnation!
Oh, you wicked fiend!
Is it a greater sin for me to break my promise?
Or is it worse to speak badly of my lord?
I use the same tongue that she used to praise him.
She praised him more than anyone else many times.
Go, counselor.
From now on, you and my heart will be two different things.
I will go to the Friar to find his remedy.
If everything else fails, I have the power to die.

raw: Exit.
